headline: Pangenome references and long reads reshape somatic variant and SV calling in cancer
label: Somatic Variant Detection Long Reads
summary: New tools call somatic SVs on tumor-normal pangenome graphs and composite references, as benchmarks show pangenome alignment improves somatic calling.
synthesis: The dominant thread is somatic variant discovery that moves beyond GRCh38-centric short-read pipelines toward long reads and sample-aware references. A published benchmark shows that graph and personalized pangenomes outperform GRCh38 for somatic variant calling. Two preprints push this into structural variation. JANUS calls somatic SVs directly on tumor-normal pangenome graphs from HiFi reads without prior alignment and reports outperforming 18 callers. VESPA-SS detects tumor-specific strings against a draft composite germline reference. At the SNV level, SomatiX applies deep learning on allele-aware pileups from matched tumor-normal long reads and outperforms DeepSomatic. Adjacent work covers complex somatic events. One study builds a multi-platform framework for somatic mobile element insertions that benchmarks long-read and MEI-targeted sequencing with phasing. Cycle-Extractor reconstructs ecDNA cycles from breakpoint graphs using MILP and outperforms AmpliconArchitect and Decoil. What is new is the use of germline-matched or graph references as the primary coordinate system for somatic analysis, rather than as a post-hoc refinement.
